footer.tagline: We build and rank websites for emergency call-out trades. Locksmiths, towing, garage doors, HVAC. Demo-first — you see it before you pay.

problem.title: The problem
problem.p1: Your customer is standing outside their own front door. It's raining. They've got one hand on a phone and four tabs open.
problem.p2: They're not reading your About page. They're looking for two things: can you actually get in, and what will it cost. Whichever site answers first gets the call.
problem.p3: Most trade sites answer neither. Big photo of a door. "Quality service since 2009." Phone number in the footer, in grey.

solution.title: What we build instead
solution.priceDesc: Not "competitive rates" — the actual call-out fee. Your customer wants a number. Give them one.
solution.arrivalDesc: Real one, from your dispatch log. "25 minutes in central, 40 minutes outer suburbs." Specifics beat promises.
solution.callTitle: A call button that never leaves
solution.callDesc: Fixed to the bottom of the viewport. Follows the thumb down the page. One tap to call, on every screen.
solution.pagesTitle: Pages for the jobs people actually search
solution.pagesDesc: Broken key extraction. Transponder programming. Panic bar repair. Someone typing "push pull paddle repair" is ready to pay today.
solution.footer: Separate pages for the areas you cover, with real detail about the buildings there. Not 200 spun copies of the same paragraph. Google's been catching that for two years.

dont.p1: We don't do logos, brand books, or social media management. We don't do e-commerce. We don't do SEO for national brands.
dont.p2: If you need a site that wins a design award, we're the wrong shop. Ours are built for a wet thumb on a cracked screen at 11pm.

faq.q: do you only build sites for locksmiths
faq.a: No. We build for any emergency call-out trade — towing, garage doors, HVAC, plumbers, electricians. Locksmiths are where we started, so we know the vertical cold.

faq.q: how long until I see something
faq.a: Three working days for the homepage. We build it on a live URL before we ask for anything.

faq.q: what if I already have a website
faq.a: We'll rebuild your homepage for free. If it's better than what you've got, we talk about finishing the site. If not, keep the files.

faq.q: do you do Google Ads for locksmiths
faq.a: Yes, in Tier 3. We manage Google Ads and Local Services Ads. Locksmith clicks run $40–$80, so budget matters — we'll tell you if your area isn't worth it.

faq.q: can you help with a suspended Google Business Profile
faq.a: We've done reinstatements. Locksmith GBP suspensions are common — Google flags the category. We know the process, but can't guarantee Google's timeline.

faq.q: what don't you do
faq.a: Logos, brand books, social media, e-commerce, national SEO. We build sites that make phones ring for local trades. That's it.

problemSection.scenario: Your customer is standing on a hard shoulder. Car won't start. It's dark, it's cold, and they've got three tabs open on a phone with 12% battery.
problemSection.searchBehavior: They don't care about your fleet photos. They want to know: can you get here, how fast, and what's it going to cost to move a 2019 Honda Civic three miles.
problemSection.whatsBroken: Most towing sites show a stock photo of a flatbed. "24/7 Towing Services." No price, no ETA, no area map. The customer calls whichever number they see first.

faq.q: do you build sites for towing companies specifically
faq.a: Yes. Towing, locksmiths, garage doors, HVAC — any emergency trade where the customer calls from a phone in a panic. Same economics, same site architecture.

faq.q: how fast can I get a site up
faq.a: Homepage in three working days. Full site in two weeks. We build it live on a real URL before you pay anything.

faq.q: do you handle Google Ads for towing
faq.a: In Tier 3, yes. Towing clicks are expensive. We'll tell you upfront if your market and budget make ads viable before we take your money.

faq.q: what about dispatch integration
faq.a: We don't build dispatch software. We build the site that makes the phone ring. If you need dispatch, we'll recommend someone, but that's not our lane.

faq.q: can you rank me for 'towing near me'
faq.a: That's a map pack result — it depends on your Google Business Profile, reviews, and proximity. Our Tier 2 builds the location pages and GBP presence that feed that ranking. Takes 4–6 months.

faq.q: I only cover a small area, is it worth it
faq.a: If you're doing 3+ jobs a day, yes. One extra call a day at your average tow fee pays for the site in a week. If your area is too thin, we'll tell you.

garage-door-websites.seoDesc: Websites for garage door repair and installation companies. Demo-first — we build it, you see it live, then decide. Local SEO, click-to-call, real pricing.

problemSection.scenario: Your customer's garage door is stuck open. It's 7am, they need to get to work, and the car is trapped inside. They're searching on their phone in the driveway.
problemSection.searchBehavior: They want three things: can you fix it today, how much is a spring replacement, and are you actually nearby. Everything else is noise.
problemSection.whatsBroken: Most garage door sites are a gallery of doors nobody asked to see. No prices, no service area, no emergency number above the fold. The call goes to whoever answers those questions.

faq.q: do you build sites for garage door companies
faq.a: Yes. Garage door repair is an emergency trade — same buying pattern as locksmith or towing. Customer's on a phone, door's broken, they call whoever looks like they can fix it today.

faq.q: what makes your sites different from a Wix template
faq.a: Specific job pages that rank for what people actually search — 'garage door spring replacement [city]' not 'our services.' Real prices on the page. A call button that follows the thumb.

faq.q: can you show pricing on the site if my prices vary
faq.a: Yes. 'Spring replacement from £85' is better than nothing. We use the 'from' price for common jobs. Customers know the final bill depends on the job — they just want to know the ballpark.

faq.q: what if I do installs too, not just repair
faq.a: We build pages for both. Repair pages are emergency-conversion pages. Install pages are more considered — different layout, before/after photos, longer copy. Same site, two modes.

faq.q: do I really need location pages
faq.a: If you serve more than one town, yes. 'Garage door repair [town name]' is how people search. One page per area you actually serve, with real detail about the buildings there.

faq.q: what don't you do
faq.a: We don't build e-commerce sites to sell doors online. We don't do social media. We don't do national SEO. We build sites that make local phones ring.

hvac-websites.seoDesc: Websites for HVAC companies — heating, cooling, emergency repair. Demo-first model. We build your site live before you pay. Local SEO and call tracking included.

problemSection.scenario: It's August. The AC died at 2pm. Your customer's house is 35°C and they've got a toddler. They're on their phone searching 'emergency AC repair' and they'll call the first number that looks real.
problemSection.searchBehavior: They don't care about your NATE certifications. They want to know: can you come today, what's the diagnostic fee, and do you work on their brand of unit.
problemSection.whatsBroken: Most HVAC sites list every service ever invented. 'Heating, cooling, ventilation, indoor air quality, ductwork, maintenance plans.' Nobody reads it. The customer wants one answer: when can you get here.

faq.q: do you build HVAC websites specifically
faq.a: Yes. HVAC is an emergency trade in summer and winter. Same site architecture as locksmith or towing — phone-first, price on the page, call button fixed to the viewport.

faq.q: what about maintenance plan signups
faq.a: We can add a maintenance plan page, but it's not the priority. The site is built to convert emergency calls first. Maintenance upsell happens on the second visit or via email follow-up.

faq.q: can you rank me for 'AC repair near me'
faq.a: That's the goal. Tier 2 builds location pages one area at a time, manages your Google Business Profile, and posts real job photos monthly. Map pack rankings take 4–6 months of consistent work.

faq.q: do you do Google Ads for HVAC
faq.a: In Tier 3. HVAC clicks are seasonal — expensive in July, cheaper in March. We'll show you the monthly cost before you commit and tell you if your area is too competitive for your budget.

faq.q: I do residential and commercial — can the site handle both
faq.a: Yes. Separate sections. Commercial leads search differently — 'commercial HVAC contractor [city]' — so they get their own pages. Residential is the emergency funnel.

faq.q: what if I'm just starting out and have no reviews
faq.a: We set up a review collection SMS flow in Tier 2. After every job, your customer gets a text with a direct link to leave a Google review. Three months of this changes everything.
